Let $R$ be a commutative ring. If $M$ is free with basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ and $N$ is free with basis $(f_j)_{j\in J}$, then $M\otimes_RN$ is free with basis

$$\bigl(e_i\otimes f_j\bigr)_{(i,j)\in I\times J}.$$

Equivalently, the canonical map $R^{(I\times J)}\to M\otimes_RN$ sending the standard basis vector at $(i,j)$ to $e_i\otimes f_j$ is an isomorphism. This includes an empty basis in either factor.

Let $V$ and $W$ be vector spaces over the same field $F$. A function
$T:V\to W$ is **linear** when

$$T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v)$$

for all $a,b\in F$ and $u,v\in V$. Such a function is a **linear map**, or
**linear transformation**.

derivations.claim: Put $\Delta=\Phi-\Psi$. By [F4], $\Delta$ is complex-linear. For every nonzero $x\in H$, $P_x=\|x\|^2P_{x/\|x\|}$, and $P_0=0$, so linearity gives $\Delta(P_x)=0$ for every $x\in H$.

With $|u\rangle\langle v|$ denoting the map $z\mapsto\langle z,v\rangle u$, the linear-first convention gives $$P_{u+v}-P_{u-v}=2(|u\rangle\langle v|+|v\rangle\langle u|)$$ and $$P_{u+iv}-P_{u-iv}=2i(|v\rangle\langle u|-|u\rangle\langle v|).$$ If $S=P_{u+v}-P_{u-v}$ and $T=P_{u+iv}-P_{u-iv}$, then $|u\rangle\langle v|=(S-T/i)/4$ and $|v\rangle\langle u|=(S+T/i)/4$. Hence $\Delta(|u\rangle\langle v|)=0$ for all $u,v$.

Choose an orthonormal basis $(e_j)$ of $H$ using [F2]. Every $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ has the expansion $T=\sum_{j,k}\langle Te_k,e_j\rangle|e_j\rangle\langle e_k|$, so these matrix units form a basis of $\mathcal B(H)$. Step 2.1 makes $\Delta$ zero on that basis, hence on all of $\mathcal B(H)$; thus $\Phi=\Psi$.

Choose an orthonormal basis $(r_a)$ of $R$. By [F3], $(e_j\otimes r_a)$ is a basis of $H\otimes R$ and the operators $|e_j\otimes r_a\rangle\langle e_k\otimes r_b|$ form a basis of $\mathcal B(H\otimes R)$. Each equals $(|e_j\rangle\langle e_k|)\otimes(|r_a\rangle\langle r_b|)$, on which $(\Delta\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(R)})$ is zero by step 2.1. Therefore the two amplified maps agree on the entire operator space.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

Let $V$ and $W$ be vector spaces over the same field $F$. A function
$T:V\to W$ is **linear** when

$$T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v)$$

for all $a,b\in F$ and $u,v\in V$. Such a function is a **linear map**, or
**linear transformation**.

Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$ ([[def-vector-space]]), let
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $v : n \to V$ be a finite list
([[def-linear-combination-and-span]]).

1. **The span of the image of a list.** Whether or not $v$ is injective,
   $$\operatorname{span}(v[n]) \;=\; \Bigl\{\, \sum_{i<n}\lambda_i v_i \;:\; \lambda : n \to F \,\Bigr\} .$$
2. **Coordinates.** $v$ is an ordered basis of $V$ ([[def-linear-basis]]) **if and
   only if** for every $x \in V$ there is **exactly one** $\lambda : n \to F$ with
   $x = \sum_{i<n}\lambda_i v_i$. When that holds, this $\lambda$ is called the
   **coordinate list of $x$ with respect to the ordered basis $v$**, and
   $\lambda_i$ its **$i$-th coordinate**.

The coordinate list is attached to the **ordered** basis and not to the basis as
a set: reordering the list permutes the coordinates of every vector, as the
companion page shows on a worked example in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$.

citations.quote: Let $\mathcal H_L,\mathcal H_P$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$ be a linear isometry. Then $V^*V=I_{\mathcal H_L}$. Consequently $P:=VV^*$ is self-adjoint and idempotent and is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}V$. If $K=\dim\mathcal H_L$ and $N=\dim\mathcal H_P$, then $0\le K\le N$; when $K=1$ the code is a line, and when $K=N$ the code subspace is all of $\mathcal H_P$ and $P=I_{\mathcal H_P}$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.
Every linear map $T:V\to W$ between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces has a unique adjoint $T^*:W\to V$.

derivations.claim: By [F2], $PV=V$, $V^*P=V^*$ and $V^*V=I_{H_L}$. Multiplying $PE_a^*E_bP=C_{ab}P$ by $V^*$ and $V$ therefore gives $V^*E_a^*E_bV=C_{ab}I_{H_L}$. Choose a unit vector $\psi\in H_L$, possible because $H_L\ne\{0\}$. The adjoint identity [F4] yields $C_{ab}=\langle E_a^*E_bV\psi,V\psi\rangle =\langle E_bV\psi,E_aV\psi\rangle$.

For any $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\in\mathbb C^m$, the first-argument linearity and conjugate symmetry in [F3] give $$z^*Cz=\sum_{a,b}\overline{z_a}z_b\langle E_bV\psi,E_aV\psi\rangle =\left\|\sum_b z_bE_bV\psi\right\|^2\ge0.$$ Also $C_{ba}=\overline{C_{ab}}$, so $C$ is Hermitian. The nonnegative quadratic form is exactly positive semidefiniteness.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.

An endomorphism $P$ of a finite-dimensional inner product space is the orthogonal projection onto some subspace if and only if

$$P^2=P\qquad\text{and}\qquad P^*=P.$$

In that case it is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}P$, along $\ker P=(\operatorname{im}P)^\perp$. The cases $P=0$ and $P=I$ are included.

Let $W$ be a subspace of a finite-dimensional inner product space $V$. The orthogonal-decomposition theorem ([[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]]) gives

$$V=W\oplus W^\perp$$

and associates to every $v\in V$ unique vectors $w\in W$ and $z\in W^\perp$ with $v=w+z$. The **orthogonal projection onto $W$** is the function

$$P_W:V\longrightarrow W,\qquad P_Wv=w.$$

Equivalently, $P_Wv$ is the unique vector of $W$ such that $v-P_Wv\in W^\perp$.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces,

$$(S+T)^*=S^*+T^*,\qquad (\lambda T)^*=\overline\lambda T^*,\qquad (ST)^*=T^*S^*,\qquad T^{**}=T.$$

Also $I^*=I$ and $0^*=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The operator $T$ is **non-negative** when $T$ is
self-adjoint in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]] and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle\ge 0$$

for every $v\in V$.

The operator $T$ is **positive** when $T$ is self-adjoint and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle>0$$

for every nonzero $v\in V$.

Let $\mathcal H_L,\mathcal H_P$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$ be a linear isometry. Then $V^*V=I_{\mathcal H_L}$. Consequently $P:=VV^*$ is self-adjoint and idempotent and is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}V$. If $K=\dim\mathcal H_L$ and $N=\dim\mathcal H_P$, then $0\le K\le N$; when $K=1$ the code is a line, and when $K=N$ the code subspace is all of $\mathcal H_P$ and $P=I_{\mathcal H_P}$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.
Every linear map $T:V\to W$ between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces has a unique adjoint $T^*:W\to V$.

the factor order $H_G\otimes H_Q$. For ordered orthonormal bases
$(g_s)$ and $(q_\alpha)$, define
$$\operatorname{Tr}_G:\mathcal B(H_G\otimes H_Q)\to\mathcal B(H_Q),\qquad (\operatorname{Tr}_G X)_{\alpha\beta}=\sum_sX_{(s,\alpha),(s,\beta)},$$
where $X_{(s,\alpha),(t,\beta)}=\langle X(g_t\otimes q_\beta),
g_s\otimes q_\alpha\rangle$ under the linear-first convention. Equivalently,
this is the partial trace over the second factor after swapping the two wires.
The partial-trace characterization and wire-permutation unitarity in
[[thm-qc-partial-trace-characterization-and-basis-independence]] and
[[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]] show that the map is independent of
the chosen orthonormal bases. In particular, the same definition applies when
$H_Q=H_L\otimes H_R$, with that residual factor order left unchanged. For an
operator on $(H_G\otimes H_L)\otimes H_R$, use the canonical associator of
the ordered tensor-register construction to view it on
$H_G\otimes(H_L\otimes H_R)$ before taking this partial trace.

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Thus every $v\in V$ has unique vectors $w\in W$ and $z\in W^\perp$ with $v=w+z$.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.

complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is

definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_aXK_a^\dagger$ be a finite Kraus representation,
where each $K_a:H\to K$. The map $\Phi$ is trace-preserving on all of
$\mathcal L(H)$, meaning $\operatorname{tr}_K(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)$
for every $X\in\mathcal L(H)$, if and only if
$$\sum_{a\in A}K_a^\dagger K_a=I_H.$$

$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

spaces. Then

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger$. Then $\Phi$ is completely positive.

orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $H$, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. The following are
equivalent: $\Phi$ is completely positive; $J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)$ is
non-negative; and $\Phi$ has a finite Kraus representation.

Let $\mathcal H_L$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\mathcal H_P=\bigotimes_{j<n}\mathcal H_j$ be a fixed ordered finite register tensor product with $n\ge1$, supplied by the QC register interface. A **quantum code** is an isometric encoding $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$. Its **code subspace** is $\mathcal C:=\operatorname{im}V$, its logical dimension is $K:=\dim\mathcal H_L$, and its physical block length is the number $n$ of tensor factors. When each physical factor is a qubit, $\mathcal H_P\cong(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$; a logical $k$-qubit register has $K=2^k$. Require $K\ge1$.

Using the root library's adjoint convention, the **code projector** is $P:=VV^*\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_P)$. The theorem [[thm-qc-isometric-encoding-projector]] proves $V^*V=I_{\mathcal H_L}$, $P^*=P=P^2$, and $\operatorname{im}P=\mathcal C$, including one-dimensional logical spaces and the full-space code.

Let $\mathcal H_L,\mathcal H_P$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$ be a linear isometry. Then $V^*V=I_{\mathcal H_L}$. Consequently $P:=VV^*$ is self-adjoint and idempotent and is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}V$. If $K=\dim\mathcal H_L$ and $N=\dim\mathcal H_P$, then $0\le K\le N$; when $K=1$ the code is a line, and when $K=N$ the code subspace is all of $\mathcal H_P$ and $P=I_{\mathcal H_P}$.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_aXK_a^\dagger$ be a finite Kraus representation,
where each $K_a:H\to K$. The map $\Phi$ is trace-preserving on all of
$\mathcal L(H)$, meaning $\operatorname{tr}_K(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)$
for every $X\in\mathcal L(H)$, if and only if
$$\sum_{a\in A}K_a^\dagger K_a=I_H.$$

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ have a finite Kraus representation
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger$. Then $\Phi$ is completely positive.

Let $V:H_L\to H_P$ be an isometry with $H_L\ne\{0\}$ and $P=VV^*$.
Let $E_1,\ldots,E_m:H_P\to H_O$ be a finite family satisfying
$PE_a^*E_bP=C_{ab}P$, and let $C$ be the resulting positive matrix.
There is a unitary matrix $U$ such that for
$F_i=\sum_aE_aU_{ai}$ one has
$\sum_iF_iXF_i^*=\sum_aE_aXE_a^*$ for every $X$, and
$V^*F_i^*F_jV=\delta_{ij}\lambda_iI_{H_L}$ with $\lambda_i\ge0$.
If $\lambda_i=0$, then $F_iV=0$; if $\lambda_i>0$, then
$W_i=F_iV/\sqrt{\lambda_i}$ is an isometry and the ranges of the $W_i$
are pairwise orthogonal.

Let $H_L,H_O$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and let
$W_i:H_L\to H_O$ be finitely many isometries with pairwise orthogonal
ranges. Then $P_i=W_iW_i^*$ are pairwise orthogonal projections, their sum
$S=\sum_iP_i$ is an orthogonal projection satisfying $0\le S\le I_{H_O}$,
and $Q=I_{H_O}-S$ is the orthogonal projection onto the residual complement.
The empty family is allowed, with $S=0$ and $Q=I_{H_O}$.
Every finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space has an orthonormal basis. In dimension zero, this is the empty basis.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.
Every linear map $T:V\to W$ between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces has a unique adjoint $T^*:W\to V$.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces,

$$(S+T)^*=S^*+T^*,\qquad (\lambda T)^*=\overline\lambda T^*,\qquad (ST)^*=T^*S^*,\qquad T^{**}=T.$$

Also $I^*=I$ and $0^*=0$.

Let $H,K,R$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, with the
library convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. For

complex-linear maps
$\Phi,\Psi:\mathcal B(H)\to\mathcal B(K)$ agree on $P_x$ for every unit
$x\in H$, then $\Phi=\Psi$ on $\mathcal B(H)$ and
$\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(R)}=
\Psi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(R)}$ on
$\mathcal B(H\otimes R)$, under the canonical matrix-unit identification.

Fix an ordered physical register $\mathcal H_P=\bigotimes_{j<n}\mathcal H_j$ with finite-dimensional factors. For $S\subseteq[n]:=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, form $\mathcal H_S$ and $\mathcal H_{S^c}$ in the inherited order, and let $\Pi_S:\mathcal H_P\to\mathcal H_S\otimes\mathcal H_{S^c}$ be the declared bijective wire permutation. An operator $E\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_P)$ is **supported in $S$** if there is $E_S\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_S)$ with

$$\Pi_S E\Pi_S^{-1}=E_S\otimes I_{S^c}.$$

Its **weight** is $\operatorname{wt}(E):=\min\{|S|:E\text{ is supported in }S\}$. The minimum exists because the full set $[n]$ supports every operator and $[n]$ has finitely many subsets. Let $\mathcal H_\varnothing=\mathbb C$; scalar identity operators have weight zero. The weight is invariant under reordering the tensor factors by their declared wire permutation ([[lem-qc-local-operator-support-is-permutation-invariant]]).

Here $E_S\otimes I_{S^c}$ is the tensor map of [[def-qc-tensor-map]]. The product factors may have arbitrary finite dimensions; qubits are the special case $\dim\mathcal H_j=2$ for every $j$.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces,

$$(S+T)^*=S^*+T^*,\qquad (\lambda T)^*=\overline\lambda T^*,\qquad (ST)^*=T^*S^*,\qquad T^{**}=T.$$

Also $I^*=I$ and $0^*=0$.

Let $(T_k:H_k\to K_k)_{k<n}$ and $(S_k:K_k\to L_k)_{k<n}$ be finite ordered
families of linear maps between finite-dimensional complex inner-product
spaces. Then

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}S_k\right)\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)=\bigotimes_{k<n}(S_kT_k),\qquad \bigotimes_{k<n}I_{H_k}=I_{\otimes_{k<n}H_k},\qquad \left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)^*=\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k^*.$$

In the first formula, $S_kT_k$ means $S_k\circ T_k$. Here $I_{H_k}$ denotes
the identity map $x\mapsto x$. All adjoints use the
repository pairing, linear in the first argument. The empty tensor-map
identity is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on $\mathbb C$.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces, with the product bases of
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For a permutation $\sigma$ of the
factor positions, the map $P_\sigma$ that reorders the factors is a bijective
linear isometry from $H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$ to
$H_{\sigma(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\sigma(n-1)}$. When source and target
are identified as the same register, $P_\sigma$ is a unitary operator in the
sense of [[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]].

Let $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$ be an isometric encoding into a fixed ordered $n$-factor register with $n\ge1$, $K:=\dim\mathcal H_L\ge1$, and code projector $P=VV^*$. An operator $E\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_P)$ is **detectable by the code** if there is a scalar $\lambda_E\in\mathbb C$ such that

$$PEP=\lambda_E P.$$

When $K\ge2$, define the **quantum distance** by

$$d:=\min\{\operatorname{wt}(E):E\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_P),\ PEP\notin\mathbb C P\},$$

where $\mathbb C P:=\{\lambda P:\lambda\in\mathbb C\}$.

When $K=1$, set $d:=n+1$ by convention; the non-detectable set is empty in that case, as proved in [[lem-qc-detectability-is-linear-and-encoding-invariant]]. The same theorem proves that the minimum for $K\ge2$ exists, the condition is linear in $E$, and changing $V$ to $VU$ for a logical unitary $U$ leaves $d$ unchanged.

This definition distinguishes detection from recovery: no recovery map or correction criterion is asserted here. In particular the distance theorem on this page only proves detection below $d$; correction maps are deferred to QC19.

For a finite-register quantum code of distance $d$, every operator $E$ with $\operatorname{wt}(E)<d$ is detectable: $PEP=\lambda_E P$ for some $\lambda_E\in\mathbb C$. No correction-map conclusion is asserted.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $V:H_L\to H_P$ be an isometry with $H_L\ne\{0\}$ and $P=VV^*$.
Let $\mathcal N(X)=\sum_{a=1}^m E_aXE_a^*$ be a finite Kraus
representation of a channel from $\mathcal B(H_P)$ to
$\mathcal B(H_O)$. If
$PE_a^*E_bP=C_{ab}P$ for all $a,b$, then there is a finite Kraus recovery
channel $\mathcal R:\mathcal B(H_O)\to\mathcal B(H_L)$ satisfying
$\mathcal R\circ\mathcal N\circ\operatorname{Ad}_V
=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_L)}$. It is obtained by diagonalizing $C$,
decoding each nonzero orthogonal error range, and sending the orthogonal
complement to a fixed logical state. For this recovery and every
$X\in\mathcal B(H_L)$, the off-diagonal error action is
$\mathcal R(E_aVX V^*E_b^*)=C_{ba}X$.

A **decoded recovery** is a channel
$\mathcal R:\mathcal B(H_O)\to\mathcal B(H_G\otimes H_L)$. The subsystem
$H_L$ is **exactly correctable** for $\mathcal N$ under $J$ when some decoded
recovery satisfies, for every finite-dimensional reference $H_R$ and every
positive semidefinite trace-one operator $\rho$ on
$(H_G\otimes H_L)\otimes H_R$,

$$((\operatorname{Tr}_G\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_R}))\circ((\mathcal R\circ\mathcal N\circ\operatorname{Ad}_J)\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_R)}))(\rho)=(\operatorname{Tr}_G\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_R)})(\rho),$$

where $\operatorname{Ad}_J(X)=JXJ^*$. The recovery may change the gauge
state. The one-operator Kraus map $\operatorname{Ad}_J$ is completely
positive by [[thm-qc-kraus-map-completely-positive]] and trace-preserving by
$J^*J=I$ and [[thm-qc-trace-preserving-kraus-normalization]]. Thus
$\Phi=\mathcal R\circ\mathcal N\circ\operatorname{Ad}_J$ is a channel
by [[thm-qc-channels-compose-and-tensor]], and it has a finite Kraus
representation by [[thm-qc-kraus-choi-equivalence]]. Explicitly, if

in the displayed recovery condition gives precisely the marginal
hypothesis of [[lem-qc-subsystem-marginal-preservation-forces-gauge-kraus-form]].

this is equivalently a corrected decoded channel of the form
$\mathcal T_G\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_L)}$ for a channel
$\mathcal T_G$ on the gauge factor. For a unit vector $g_0\in H_G$, resetting

A **quantum code** is an isometric encoding $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$. Its **code subspace** is $\mathcal C:=\operatorname{im}V$, its logical dimension is $K:=\dim\mathcal H_L$, and its physical block length is the number $n$ of tensor factors. When each physical factor is a qubit, $\mathcal H_P\cong(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$; a logical $k$-qubit register has $K=2^k$. Require $K\ge1$.

Using the root library's adjoint convention, the **code projector** is $P:=VV^*\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_P)$. The theorem [[thm-qc-isometric-encoding-projector]] proves $V^*V=I_{\mathcal H_L}$, $P^*=P=P^2$, and $\operatorname{im}P=\mathcal C$, including one-dimensional logical spaces and the full-space code.

Let $\mathcal H_L,\mathcal H_P$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$ be a linear isometry. Then $V^*V=I_{\mathcal H_L}$. Consequently $P:=VV^*$ is self-adjoint and idempotent and is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}V$. If $K=\dim\mathcal H_L$ and $N=\dim\mathcal H_P$, then $0\le K\le N$; when $K=1$ the code is a line, and when $K=N$ the code subspace is all of $\mathcal H_P$ and $P=I_{\mathcal H_P}$.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])

with the root convention that

([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists

defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in

Every finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space has an orthonormal basis. In dimension zero, this is the empty basis.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

$$(S+T)^*=S^*+T^*,\qquad (\lambda T)^*=\overline\lambda T^*,\qquad (ST)^*=T^*S^*,\qquad T^{**}=T.$$

$x\in H$, then $\Phi=\Psi$ on $\mathcal B(H)$ and
$\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(R)}=

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**

$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $(T_k:H_k\to K_k)_{k<n}$ and $(S_k:K_k\to L_k)_{k<n}$ be finite ordered
families of linear maps between finite-dimensional complex inner-product
spaces. Then

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}S_k\right)\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)=\bigotimes_{k<n}(S_kT_k),\qquad \bigotimes_{k<n}I_{H_k}=I_{\otimes_{k<n}H_k},\qquad \left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)^*=\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k^*.$$

In the first formula, $S_kT_k$ means $S_k\circ T_k$. Here $I_{H_k}$ denotes
the identity map $x\mapsto x$. All adjoints use the
repository pairing, linear in the first argument. The empty tensor-map
identity is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on $\mathbb C$.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

Let $H_G,H_Q$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with fixed
ordered orthonormal bases $(g_s)_{s<m}$ and $(q_\alpha)_{\alpha<n}$; either
index set may be empty. Put $\mathcal B(H)=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(H)$.
For each $s,t<m$ and $\alpha,\beta<n$, define
$$M_{s\alpha,t\beta}x=\langle x,g_t\otimes q_\beta\rangle(g_s\otimes q_\alpha).$$
Then the family $(M_{s\alpha,t\beta})_{s,t,\alpha,\beta}$ is a basis of
$\mathcal B(H_G\otimes H_Q)$. If either factor is zero-dimensional, this is
the empty basis of the zero endomorphism space.

derivations.claim: For necessity, let $\mathcal R:\mathcal B(H_O)\to\mathcal B(H_G\otimes H_L)$ be an exact decoded recovery. By [F3], choose a finite Kraus family $(S_r)$ for $\mathcal R$. The corrected map $\Phi=\mathcal R\circ\mathcal N\circ\operatorname{Ad}_J$ has Kraus operators $K_{ra}=S_rE_aJ$. It is completely positive by [F3], and $$\sum_{r,a}K_{ra}^*K_{ra} =J^*\sum_aE_a^*\left(\sum_rS_r^*S_r\right)E_aJ =J^*\left(\sum_aE_a^*E_a\right)J =J^*J=I_{H_G\otimes H_L}$$ by [F2] and [F3]. Thus $\Phi$ is a channel. By exactness [F1], it preserves the $H_L$ marginal; [F4] gives $S_rE_aJ=A_{ra}\otimes I_{H_L}$ for some $A_{ra}:H_G\to H_G$.

For sufficiency, assume $J^*E_a^*E_bJ=M_{ab}\otimes I_{H_L}$. Let $d_G=\dim H_G>0$ and choose an orthonormal basis $(g_k)_{k<d_G}$ by [F7]. Define $\iota_k:H_L\to H_G\otimes H_L$ by $\iota_kx=g_k\otimes x$, and put $F_{ak}=E_aJ\iota_k$ and $\widetilde F_{ak}=F_{ak}/\sqrt{d_G}$. By trace preservation [F3] and $J^*J=I$ from [F2], $$\sum_{a,k}F_{ak}^*F_{ak} =\sum_k\iota_k^*J^*\left(\sum_aE_a^*E_a\right)J\iota_k =d_G I_{H_L}.$$ Thus $(\widetilde F_{ak})$ is a finite Kraus representation of a channel $\widetilde{\mathcal N}:\mathcal B(H_L)\to\mathcal B(H_O)$.

Trace preservation of $\mathcal R$ and $\mathcal N$ gives $\sum_rS_r^*S_r=I_{H_O}$ and $\sum_aE_a^*E_a=I_{H_P}$ by [F3]. Hence $$J^*E_a^*E_bJ =J^*E_a^*\left(\sum_rS_r^*S_r\right)E_bJ =\sum_r(S_rE_aJ)^*(S_rE_bJ) =\left(\sum_rA_{ra}^*A_{rb}\right)\otimes I_{H_L}.$$ Set $M_{ab}=\sum_rA_{ra}^*A_{rb}$. This proves the operator-valued condition.

For all $a,b,k,\ell$, the assumed condition gives $$\widetilde F_{ak}^*\widetilde F_{b\ell} =\frac{\langle M_{ab}g_\ell,g_k\rangle}{d_G}I_{H_L}.$$ Apply [F5] to $\widetilde{\mathcal N}$ with the identity encoding of $H_L$. It supplies a channel $\mathcal S:\mathcal B(H_O)\to\mathcal B(H_L)$ and a finite Kraus family $(S_r)$ for which $$\mathcal S(\widetilde F_{ak}X\widetilde F_{b\ell}^*) =\frac{\langle M_{ba}g_k,g_\ell\rangle}{d_G}X$$ for every $X\in\mathcal B(H_L)$.

Fix an orthonormal gauge basis $(g_k)$ using [F7]. The matrix entry of $M_{ab}$ in row $k$, column $\ell$ is $\langle M_{ab}g_\ell,g_k\rangle$ by [F8]. Therefore $$P_{kk}E_a^*E_bP_{\ell\ell} =J\bigl(Q_{kk}(M_{ab}\otimes I_{H_L})Q_{\ell\ell}\bigr)J^* =\langle M_{ab}g_\ell,g_k\rangle P_{k\ell}.$$ This proves the matrix-unit statement in the necessary direction.

Trace preservation and $J^*J=I$ imply $$\sum_aM_{aa}\otimes I_{H_L} =J^*\left(\sum_aE_a^*E_a\right)J =I_{H_G\otimes H_L},$$ so $\sum_aM_{aa}=I_{H_G}$: applying the equality to each $g\otimes\ell_0$ for fixed unit $\ell_0$ gives $(\sum_aM_{aa}g-g)\otimes\ell_0=0$, and tensoring with nonzero $\ell_0$ is injective. Define the decoded recovery $\mathcal T(X)=P_{g_0}\otimes\mathcal S(X)$ for a fixed unit $g_0\in H_G$. For a gauge matrix unit $|g_k\rangle\langle g_\ell|\otimes X$, the encoded channel output is $\sum_aF_{ak}XF_{a\ell}^*$; applying $\mathcal S$ and scaling the cross-term formula in step 2.2 from $\widetilde F_{ak}$ to $F_{ak}=\sqrt{d_G}\,\widetilde F_{ak}$ gives logical output $$\sum_a\mathcal S(F_{ak}XF_{a\ell}^*) =\sum_a\langle M_{aa}g_k,g_\ell\rangle X =\langle g_k,g_\ell\rangle X =\delta_{k\ell}X.$$ Here the scaling is $\mathcal S(F_{ak}XF_{b\ell}^*)=d_G\mathcal S(\widetilde F_{ak}X\widetilde F_{b\ell}^*)$, so the factor $d_G$ cancels the denominator in step 2.2. The input logical marginal of that matrix unit is also $\delta_{k\ell}X$. By linearity and the product matrix-unit basis in [F12], the decoded map $\mathcal T$ with output gauge reset preserves the logical marginal on every operator; [F9] extends the equality to every finite reference.

Since $P=JJ^*$, the operator-valued condition gives $PE_a^*E_bP=J(M_{ab}\otimes I_{H_L})J^*$. Conversely, multiplying this compressed equality by $J^*$ and $J$ and using $J^*J=I$ recovers the operator-valued condition.

The Kraus operators of $\mathcal T$ are $T_r y=g_0\otimes S_r y$. Since $g_0$ is unit, $\sum_rT_r^*T_r=\sum_rS_r^*S_r=I_{H_O}$; hence $\mathcal T$ is a channel by [F3]. Step 3.2 proves it preserves the logical marginal on every operator, and [F9] extends that identity to every finite reference. The physical reset-and-encode map is a channel by [F4], so the protected subsystem is exactly correctable.

For a fixed orthonormal gauge basis, if the operator-valued condition holds, then $Q_{kk}(J^*E_a^*E_bJ)Q_{\ell\ell} =\langle M_{ab}g_\ell,g_k\rangle Q_{k\ell}$, which gives the embedded matrix-unit condition after multiplying by $J$ and $J^*$. Conversely, sum the embedded matrix-unit identities over $k,\ell$. Since $\sum_kP_{kk}=P$ and $J^*P_{k\ell}J=Q_{k\ell}$, the resulting operator is $J^*E_a^*E_bJ=(\sum_{k,\ell}\lambda_{abk\ell}|g_k\rangle\langle g_\ell|)\otimes I_{H_L}$. This establishes equivalence for the fixed basis; because the operator-valued condition is basis-independent, it holds for every orthonormal gauge basis.

If $\dim H_G=1$, every $M_{ab}$ is a scalar, so the criterion becomes $PE_a^*E_bP=C_{ab}P$. Under the unitary identification $H_G\otimes H_L\cong H_L$, the first-factor trace leaves the logical operator unchanged, so the subsystem recovery definition [F11] is ordinary exact recovery. The necessity and sufficiency directions are [F6].

Let $\mathcal H_L$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\mathcal H_P=\bigotimes_{j<n}\mathcal H_j$ be a fixed ordered finite register tensor product with $n\ge1$, supplied by the QC register interface. A **quantum code** is an isometric encoding $V:\mathcal H_L\to\mathcal H_P$. Its **code subspace** is $\mathcal C:=\operatorname{im}V$, its logical dimension is $K:=\dim\mathcal H_L$, and its physical block length is the number $n$ of tensor factors. When each physical factor is a qubit, $\mathcal H_P\cong(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$; a logical $k$-qubit register has $K=2^k$. Require $K\ge1$.

Using the root library's adjoint convention, the **code projector** is $P:=VV^*\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_P)$. The theorem [[thm-qc-isometric-encoding-projector]] proves $V^*V=I_{\mathcal H_L}$, $P^*=P=P^2$, and $\operatorname{im}P=\mathcal C$, including one-dimensional logical spaces and the full-space code.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ have a finite Kraus representation
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger$. Then $\Phi$ is completely positive.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_aXK_a^\dagger$ be a finite Kraus representation,
where each $K_a:H\to K$. The map $\Phi$ is trace-preserving on all of
$\mathcal L(H)$, meaning $\operatorname{tr}_K(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)$
for every $X\in\mathcal L(H)$, if and only if
$$\sum_{a\in A}K_a^\dagger K_a=I_H.$$

Let $V:H_L\to H_P$ be an isometry with $H_L\ne\{0\}$ and $P=VV^*$.
Let $\mathcal N(X)=\sum_{a=1}^m E_aXE_a^*$ be a finite Kraus
representation of a channel from $\mathcal B(H_P)$ to
$\mathcal B(H_O)$. If
$PE_a^*E_bP=C_{ab}P$ for all $a,b$, then there is a finite Kraus recovery
channel $\mathcal R:\mathcal B(H_O)\to\mathcal B(H_L)$ satisfying
$\mathcal R\circ\mathcal N\circ\operatorname{Ad}_V
=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_L)}$. It is obtained by diagonalizing $C$,
decoding each nonzero orthogonal error range, and sending the orthogonal
complement to a fixed logical state. For this recovery and every
$X\in\mathcal B(H_L)$, the off-diagonal error action is
$\mathcal R(E_aVX V^*E_b^*)=C_{ba}X$.

derivations.claim: Both $I_4$ and $X\otimes I_2$ are unitary, so $E_0^*E_0+E_1^*E_1=I_4$. The map $\mathcal N(Y)=E_0YE_0^*+E_1YE_1^*$ is therefore a channel.

By the definitions of $V$ and $W$, $W^*V=0$, $V^*V=W^*W=I_L$, and $$(V^*E_a^*E_bV)_{a,b} =\begin{pmatrix}I_L/2&0\\0&I_L/2\end{pmatrix}.$$ The normalized error restrictions are $V$ and $W$, so their ranges are orthogonal and each syndrome has weight $1/2$.
Define recovery Kraus operators $R_0=V^*$ and $R_1=W^*$. Then $R_0^*R_0+R_1^*R_1=VV^*+WW^*=I_4$, so the recovery is trace-preserving.

The only nonzero corrected error products are $R_0E_0V=I_L/\sqrt2$ and $R_1E_1V=I_L/\sqrt2$. Hence for every $Y\in\mathcal B(H_L)$ the corrected channel returns $\frac12Y+\frac12Y=Y$. This is the orthogonal-syndrome branch of [F3].
